event.summary: Refresh can be silently reduced to a cached read
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: clicking Refresh while a container-place read is already running can leave the displayed host readiness stale because no new host probe is requested. Details: environment_ui.rs:684-704 captures the refresh flag in the closure supplied to request_read and clears it with mem::take. reader.rs:643-670 returns immediately when claim fails and drives all follow-up reads using the original closure. A feed/scheduled cached read captures false; Refresh during it records Explicit demand but drops the new true closure, so the follow-up only fetches cached places. Likewise a second Refresh during the mount refresh is lost after the first mem::take. The explicit Refresh control at containers_settings.rs:59-63 invokes this route. SPEC_impl.md, Podman places, creation and images, defines probes as background refreshes and cached availability; a cached fetch does not repeat the probe. Source-confirmed, no execution. Suggested bucket: other (intermittently ineffective refresh and stale readiness, no established loss-of-work or security route). Could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Fix direction: retain pending refresh demand in component-owned state sampled by each actual reader dispatch rather than a discarded per-trigger closure. Preserve separate cached reads and explicit host-probe admission.

event.summary: Refresh can be silently reduced to a cached read
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: clicking Refresh while a container-place read is running can leave changed container-host readiness stale because the requested host probe is never sent. Source-confirmed through synthesis, no execution. environment_ui.rs:693-704 captures refresh in the per-trigger closure and consumes it at :698. reader.rs:444-456 records Explicit demand but returns false while running; :651-659 then drops the arriving closure and reuses the old closure for subsequent reads. finish at :512-537 does honor the queued demand immediately, so this is not a lost demand flag or missing retry: the wrong operation (cached GET) answers it. ContainersSettings :52-63 leaves Refresh enabled during reads (only deletion busy disables it), making the overlap a shipped control sequence. api/environments.rs:6-14 is cached GET; :103-112 alone sends the explicit probe POSTs. hosts.rs:4294-4339 auto-probes only never-checked hosts, not checked hosts whose cached capability reason has become stale. A concrete source route needs no failed request, recipe job or missing event: after opening probes settle, a fleet notice starts a cached GET for an already checked host; a Refresh click during that GET queues only another cached GET. Subsequent feed/fallback reads also carry false. GET success hides any preceding request error but proves no fresh probe. The related failure variant remains: true is consumed before awaits, so a failed explicit refresh can retry as GET without completing the probe POSTs. Recovery and limits: Refresh during a reader backoff claims a new reader and keeps true; Refresh when idle also works. Closing/reopening Settings or opening a new launcher mounts a fresh hook and requests true. Settings section switching only hides its mounted components, so it does not rerun the mount refresh. New/unprobed hosts may still auto-probe on GET. An already admitted probe may independently complete and mask the issue; the established route uses a previously settled cache. The 300-second probe freshness bound is checked by backend reuse, not by the cached display GET, so it is not a timed UI repair. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Podman places, creation and images, and hook docs :684-688 distinguish cached reads from opening/explicit probe refresh. Suggested bucket: other; intermittent ineffective refresh and stale readiness, with no established security or work-loss route. Could-be-highest:no. proposed_drop:false. possible_cover: parent-provided g060/l1 and g061/l5 are related but distinct: RecipeList's place_status is a separate Resource for /api/recipe-places (tensorlake/recipes.rs:375-385); job completion invalidation concerns registry removal (tensorlake/build.rs:446-449). Neither is required for this /api/environment-places plus probe-POST failure. Fix direction: retain probe-refresh demand in component-owned state sampled by each dispatch, and clear it only at the intended completion boundary, rather than keeping its only bit in a discarded/spent trigger closure. This preserves the original stale-readiness consequence without claiming permanent unavailability.

event.summary: Container-start explanation promises interrupted status for every session
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. Discovery pass 1. TLDR: when Farhelm starts a stopped container, its explanation says the sessions return as interrupted with Restart available, even for sessions that already ended and must retain their known result. This misstates what recovery will do. Source: ProviderUi::starting_help at environment_ui.rs:261-271 unconditionally says "Starting the container again; its sessions return as interrupted, with Restart available." resume_help at :249-252 reuses it for the stopped-container Resume tooltip. Actual shipped callers: sandbox_sessions.rs:124-130 installs this as the session unavailable-card explanation for starting:true; :345 uses resume_help for a Stopped host. session_view.rs:2022-2024 chooses that notice for stale/frozen session-owned hosts, and :2357-2363 mounts Controls whenever sandbox_host exists, without excluding an already-ended session. manager.rs:3841-3890 automatically starts a Stopped environment once its place is connected, independently of whether cached sessions already ended. Thus a previously exited session retained in a stopped container can receive the unconditional guidance during the automatic start or the explicit Resume route. Exact contract, SPEC.md:4786-4789: "Successful start brings back its supervisor with ordinary session classification. A host reboot interrupts sessions last known live, while known exits keep their outcome. A container stopped and started on the same host boot returns ended sessions through ordinary exit classification. event.summary: Container-leftover Delete opens its question without focusing an answer
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. Discovery pass 1. TLDR: opening a container-leftover Delete question leaves keyboard focus on the old list button instead of moving into the question. Keyboard users must find the answers themselves; another Enter on the still-focused Delete just opens a replacement question. Source: containers_settings.rs:112-126 keeps the row button mounted and enabled and its handler only clears action_error and calls confirm.open(row.clone(),()). The inline alertdialog at :130-178 supplies neither autofocus nor an onmounted/use_effect focus handoff for either Cancel or Delete container. These are all the component's hooks and answer controls. Settings itself is already mounted; settings.rs:329-339 installs its root with remembered Sessions/close focus. modal_dialog.rs:957-967 explicitly keeps child focus handoffs independent and ordinary rerenders from repeating initial focus; :999-1006 invokes handle.install only on root mount. modal_isolation.rs:176-191 permits existing focus anywhere inside that Settings root and does not move focus from the retained row; its observer at :202-213 only claims outside siblings, not new alertdialog answers. The scroll-region recovery at modal_dialog.rs:589-614 likewise refuses recovery while a usable current control owns focus. Thus the generic boundary does not supply the missing question handoff. Exact applicable contract, SPEC.md Keyboard focus, Opening and closing (:3246-3252): "A confirmation the user just opened starts on the action they asked for: focus starts on its enabled confirming button"; it then separately says "A risky action that cannot be undone starts on Cancel instead, as the YOLO confirmation does." This irreversible whole-container cleanup should at least focus the appropriate answer (Cancel under the irreversible rule), not keep focus on its old opener. Correction to the initial lead: the defect is absence of any question-answer focus handoff; it is not a demand to focus the risky Delete answer contrary to that exception. Other sandbox orphan confirmations also predate this focus policy, but this assigned new component creates its own new noncompliant route during the review range; pre-existing similar behavior is no refutation. Suggested bucket: other, keyboard navigation/focus contract defect. Could-be-highest:no established destructive mis-targeting, automatic confirmation, security or work-loss route; retained focus is on the opener, which reopens rather than deletes. Confidence: confirmed through source and contract analysis, not execution. proposed_drop:false. possible_cover:none in supplied neighbour projection. Fix direction: add an opening-bound focus handoff to the question's intended initial answer, preserving repeated/composing Enter guards and captured ConfirmToken answers. No runtime tests, reproductions or live-install actions.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. Discovery pass 2. TLDR: an unregistered container cleanup failure disappears when Settings closes. Reopening shows the leftover and a fresh Delete button without the prior failure reason; closing before the request finishes can discard its only visible failure report entirely. Source: containers_settings.rs:46 stores action_error only in the component. The admitted delete survives closing (:165-167), but :168-170 returns before handling its result when unmounted; while mounted :174 records the failure only in that local signal. Neither reads nor row rendering restore operation failures. ContainerLeftoverView (proto/environment.rs:157-166) has id/name/place/role/host and no cleanup result; podman.rs:828-834 constructs that bare view from ownership discovery. For the concrete unregistered route (row.host=None), api/environments.rs:80-89 uses DELETE /api/container-orphans. Its handler environment/podman.rs:876-907 runs owned cleanup but returns failure only as a 502 body, without retaining a failed operation. Provider delete_leftover at :725-763 revalidates identity/ownership then calls remove_container; its errors do not create a host record or another diagnostic owner. A later successful discovery therefore recovers the remaining resource, not its previous failure reason.
